patches.provenance: STRUCTURAL, confirmed on Gallica f53 (corners 105/106) right column, bottom quarter, at 2x. Migne repeats the guillemet at the head of each continued line: « Ex / « omnibus animantibus mundis tolles septena et se- / « ptena, » etc. Our twin drops both repeats. Ink cannot destroy a printed mark, so a single good read settles it. NOTE the archive stint's own reading of this line (`tolles septe-«ptena`) is WRONG — Gallica prints `septena et se-`/`ptena` in full, exactly the twin's word. The second repeat falls inside a word CC has already joined, so it is set before the joined word.

patches.provenance: STRUCTURAL (source loss), confirmed on Gallica f59 right column, quarter C, at 2x. The plate prints: id est, civitas quatuor; קרית CHARIAT enim Hebraice civitas, ארבע arbe quatuor. Two Hebrew words are lost in our twin, and the loss has fused Migne's italic phrases: the italic ends at *quatuor* before the semicolon, resumes at *civitas* alone, and resumes again at *arbe quatuor*. Reading of ארבע follows the archive stint's consonants; possible pointing under the bet is not resolvable even at 12x and is not reproduced.

Confirmed on Gallica f60 (corners 119/120) right column, quarter D, at 2x and at 8x: the plate prints a semicolon, not a comma, inside the Tit 1:12 quotation. Both witnesses agree against the twin, and at 8x the upper dot and lower comma of the semicolon are separately resolved. Migne sets it with his usual French space before the mark; the space is not reproduced.
